summary.en-US: Unofficial local file actions for Immich asset pages.

description.en-US:
Immich Bridge is an unofficial integration for Immich and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Immich project.

It adds a toolbar button to your configured Immich web app so you can reveal mapped local assets in Windows Explorer, copy the original file to the clipboard, or open it with desktop applications. Photos stored in Immich's own upload library, and photos with Immich edits applied, are opened as read-only copies so the originals are never changed.

This add-on requires the Immich Bridge desktop companion app for local file actions. Install the companion app from the latest GitHub release: https://github.com/Peaj/immich-bridge/releases/latest

Browser extensions cannot directly open Windows Explorer or launch arbitrary desktop applications, so the companion app handles those OS-level actions. The add-on talks to it through native messaging, which lets it show whether the companion app is installed and up to date. Older companion versions keep working through the immich-bridge:// protocol.

The extension only runs on the Immich URL you configure. When you click an Immich Bridge action, it reads the selected Immich asset's original path and passes only that path to the locally installed companion app. For read-only copies, it downloads the photo from your Immich server with your existing session and hands the file only to the local companion app. It does not send page content, asset paths, telemetry, or any other data to remote servers.

version.approval_notes: Immich Bridge is an unofficial integration for Immich and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Immich project. This extension injects one toolbar button into the Immich web app origin configured by the user. Local file actions are delegated to the separately installed Immich Bridge desktop companion app because browser extensions cannot directly open Windows Explorer or launch arbitrary desktop applications. The nativeMessaging permission connects to that companion app's native host (de.peaj.immich_bridge), which the companion app registers for this add-on ID only. The background script sends it the clicked asset's original path and the action name, and asks for its version and supported actions. If the companion app is older or missing, the extension falls back to the immich-bridge:// protocol. For photos stored in Immich's own upload library, and for copies with Immich's edits applied, the content script downloads the file from the user's configured Immich server with the user's existing session and streams it through the background script to the local companion app, which saves it as a read-only copy. The file is only ever sent to the local companion app. The options page also uses native messaging, directly from the extension page, to show and edit the folder mappings stored in the companion app's local config file and to ask the companion to find a pasted Immich file path on the user's drives. The background script never relays these messages from web pages. The manifest declares websiteContent because the extension reads the selected Immich asset's originalPath from the user's configured Immich web app and passes that single path to the local desktop companion app only after a user click. No website content is transmitted to a remote server, and there is no telemetry. The extension stores only the configured Immich origin in local browser storage.
